documentsNote: Documents are hosted on SharePoint for registered participants. If you have trouble opening them, contact the organisers.

venue.name: GIZ Campus Forum, Auditorium
venue._addressNote: Per logistical note of 13 Nov 2026: all four days at GIZ Campus Forum, Auditorium. Meeting rooms for side meetings and bilaterals on request.

gettingThere: From the airport (Cologne Bonn or Frankfurt): take a train or bus to Bonn Central Station (Bonn Hbf). Tickets are sold at bahn.com/en, in the DB Navigator app, at the DB travel centre or from ticket machines.

From Bonn Hbf: take underground tram (U-Bahn) line 16 or 63 towards Bad Godesberg, or line 66 towards Bad Honnef, and get off at Ollenhauerstraße. Turn right onto Friedrich-Ebert-Allee and walk towards the city centre; GIZ is on the left.

Fares are paid by participants. For a full week, a weekly ticket (Wochenticket) for price level 1b is usually cheapest; the Deutschlandticket is also valid. Paper tickets bought from a machine outside the tram must be stamped.
Hotels in the Bundesviertel or near Bonn Hbf give the easiest access to the venue. Participants book their own accommodation unless it is covered by other means.

sections.heading: Attending
sections.body: Energy Planning Week 2026 runs in a hybrid format. Registration is currently open for online participation only. On-site places (up to 120) are confirmed directly by the co-hosts, with priority for speakers, government planners, and members and partners of the LTES Network, GCEP and GET.transform. All plenary and numbered sessions are streamed on Microsoft Teams, except the closed-door strategic meeting on Day 2.

sections.heading: Registration and badges
sections.body: Registration and badge collection open at 08:00 on Tuesday 1 December at the GIZ Campus. Bring a valid photo ID (passport or national identity card); your badge is needed to enter the venue all week. Photographs and video will be taken during the event and may be published by IRENA and GET.transform; participants sign a consent form when collecting their badge.

sections.heading: Meals
sections.body: Breakfast, coffee breaks and a vegetarian lunch (with a vegan option) are provided free of charge to registered on-site participants on all four days. Registered on-site participants are invited to a vegetarian welcome dinner on Tuesday 1 December, 19:00–21:00, at Eventmanufaktur near Bonn Central Station. A reception follows Day 3 on Thursday 3 December. Please send any dietary restrictions to LTES@irena.org as soon as possible.

sections.heading: Visas and letters
sections.body: Participants who need a Schengen visa to enter Germany should apply as early as possible: appointments in some countries are booked months ahead. IRENA can provide a visa support letter for participants attending in person on request; contact LTES@irena.org. Passport details are requested separately, and only once your place is confirmed. Please do not send them by email.

sections.heading: Access and language
sections.body: Sessions run in English only, without interpretation. Let the organisers know in advance if you have accessibility requirements.

sections.heading: Weather, power and time
sections.body: Bonn in early December is cold and often wet, typically 0–7 °C: bring a warm coat and an umbrella. Germany uses type C and F plugs (230 V, 50 Hz); bring an adapter if needed. Bonn is on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1).
